name: Strange-tailed Tyrant
rangeDescription: Locally in eastern paraguay, southern brazil, uruguay, and northern argentina
description: Striking flycatcher with a spectacular mating display, in which male flies high into the air and repeatedly pumps tails above and then below body. Endemic to the Iberá marshes of NE Argentina and E Paraguay.

name: Chestnut-crowned Sparrow-Weaver
rangeDescription: Senegal to sudan, ethiopia, northern uganda, and northwestern kenya
description: A large weaver with bold and distinctive patterning. Note the mostly rufous head, the white throat and eyebrow, and the black moustache.

name: Taiwan Liocichla
rangeDescription: Montane forest of taiwan
description: The gloom of the forest may make this small songbird of dense montane forests and edges appear dark, but a bit of sunlight reveals a gloriously colorful plumage, with subtle patches of olive, blue, yellow, orange, and chestnut. Social, moving about in pairs or flocks, often emerging out into the open when gaps in the vegetation are present.

name: Pohnpei White-eye
rangeDescription: Pohnpei (eastern caroline islands)
description: Small gray bird endemic to Pohnpei, in the Caroline Islands of Micronesia. Uniform plumage makes it unmistakable on the island; Caroline Islands White-eye is yellowish overall, while Long-billed White-eye is greenish with a much longer bill.

name: Gray-hooded Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (espírito santo) to eastern paraguay and northeastern argentina
description: Small flycatcher that is largely olive above and cinnamon below with a gray head. The bill is two-toned with a pale base.

name: Chusquea Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Andes of southern ecuador to far northern peru (eastern piura and northern cajamarca)
description: Drab, mouse-like bird found in high-elevation cloud forest along the east slope of the Andes in southern Ecuador and far northern Peru. Plumage is gray with brown on lower back, wings, vent, and tail.

name: Rufous-tailed Rock-Thrush
rangeDescription: Rocky regions of southern palearctic region; winters to eastern africa
description: Distinctive, small, short-tailed thrush-like bird. Males are strikingly beautiful with bright blue-gray head, white back patch, and chestnut underparts.

name: Pied Coucal
rangeDescription: New ireland and new britain (eastern bismarck archipelago)
description: A long-tailed, thick-billed, uniquely patterned bird with dark blue wings, tail, and belly and creamy neck, chest, and head. Note the obvious dark cap and mask.

name: Bryan's Shearwater
rangeDescription: Range poorly known; discovered on midway island (hawaii), but probably breeds bonin islands (japan)
description: Smallest known shearwater. Tiny, black and white shearwater with rapidly fluttering wingbeats and an entirely white face.

name: American Golden-Plover
rangeDescription: Breeds alaska and northern canada; winters in southern south america, primarily in eastern argentina and adjacent paraguay and southern brazil
description: Slender, long-winged plover usually found in relatively dry habitats. Breeding plumage shows black belly and face, white neck sides, and dark back and crown spangled with gold.

name: White-bellied Tit
rangeDescription: Southeastern nigeria and central cameroon; southeastern south sudan southward to tanzania
description: A mostly black tit with a white belly and white marks in the wings. Found in rather moist savanna and woodland and along forest edges, mostly at middle and higher elevations.

name: Ticking Doradito
rangeDescription: Breeds central chile, and western argentina; winters northward to bolivia
description: Very local little bird of fresh and brackish marshes and adjacent weedy vegetation in lowlands. Departs Chile in the winter (mainly late March to mid-October) for unknown areas east of the Andes.

name: Woodwards' Batis
rangeDescription: Southern malawi to eastern zimbabwe, mozambique, and kwazulu-natal
description: A cute, dumpy, colorful flycatcher-like bird with a diffuse buff breast that distinguishes it from other batises in its range. The sexes differ: the male has a white wing bar and pale throat; the female has a buffy wing bar and buffy throat.

name: Malayan Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: High mountains of peninsular thailand and malay peninsula
description: Predominantly cinnamon-brown, this attractive laughingthrush also has olive-yellow wings, silvery cheeks and nape, and a thin but bright white eye-ring. Moves actively in pairs or small flocks on or near the ground in the dense undergrowth of montane forests.

name: Oriental Magpie
rangeDescription: Southeastern russia, northeastern china, and korea southward through eastern china, taiwan, and hainan to northern myanmar, northern laos, and northern vietnam
description: Conspicuous black-and-white bird with a long tail; wings and tail shine with green and blue gloss in good lighting. A common inhabitant of open and semi-open habitats such as fields and farmlands, often seen perched up on power lines or fence posts.

name: Blackish Oystercatcher
rangeDescription: Northern peru to tierra del fuego and falkland islands; winters to uruguay
description: Distinctive large chunky shorebird of rocky coasts, adjacent sandy beaches and river mouths. The only all-dark oystercatcher in South America, readily identified by wholly dark plumage, long orange-red bill, thick pinkish legs.

name: Tanimbar Starling
rangeDescription: Tanimbar islands (larat and yamdena)
description: A uniformly blackish starling with a medium-length square tail and a dark eye. Juveniles browner, with streaking below and a rufous-tinged tail.

name: Harlequin Duck
rangeDescription: Breeds eastern siberia and northern japan, alaska southward to oregon and wyoming, eastern canada (southeastern baffin island southward to the gulf of st. lawrence), greenland and iceland; winters coastally from siberia to japan and korea, from alaska to central california, to the northeastern usa, southern greenland, and iceland
description: Fairly small, boldly patterned diving duck that lives a seemingly dangerous life near fast-moving water and jagged rocks. Male is striking and unmistakable.

name: Crab-Plover
rangeDescription: Coastal northern indian ocean; ranges to madagascar and andaman islands
description: Utterly unmistakable large shorebird: gleaming white adult has a black back, black flight feathers, and a very heavy dark bill, which is used to dispatch crustaceans and other invertebrates. Narrow dark smudge around the eye imparts a sleepy appearance.

name: Ayeyarwady Bulbul
rangeDescription: Central and southern myanmar
description: Dull brown bulbul with streaky patch over the ears. Very similar in appearance to Streak-eared Bulbul but browner and with dull red (not pale gray) eyes.
